issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal): the problem statement (UML and prose) specifies that calculateTotalPrice should return a double (to calculate the net cost with double precision), but the solution implementation declares calculateTotalPrice as returning an int (public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)). This mismatch between the specified return type (double) and the implemented return type (int) creates an inconsistency that will confuse students about the expected method signature and numeric precision and may cause compilation or test integration issues when graders/tests expect the double signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem specification: change the method signature in SealSaloon to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and compute the sum using a double (e.g., double sum = 0.0) so the method returns a double. Ensure any additions to sum use double arithmetic (cast or use double variables). Alternatively, if integer prices are intended, update the problem statement/UML to specify an int return type, but prefer returning double to match the stated requirement for double precision.
